headlines.title: Jensen Huang is out and Nvidia stock is down—what market pros say about buying dips
headlines.summary: Jensen Huang's confirmed departure is the single biggest single-name event on the tape this week — NVDA has shed nearly $500 billion in market cap, dragging the SOX, QQQ, and every AI-adjacent name with it. This isn't just a chip story; it's touching AI financing, neocloud credit, the Anthropic IPO pipeline, and U.S.-China relations all at once. The rotation into AMD, Broadcom, and TSMC tells you the Street is repricing the whole sector, not just one stock.

headlines.title: The Fed expected rate cuts this year. Now it's bracing for another inflation fight
headlines.summary: October CPI came in hotter than expected at 0.4% month-over-month, and now the Fed — which was supposed to be cutting — is staring down another hike cycle. The long bond is getting hit, the dollar is near a 19-month high, and the yen is testing 160; that's a global rates repricing, not a domestic footnote. Every rate-sensitive sector from housing to utilities to growth tech is in the crosshairs when the Fed pivots from dove to hawk.

headlines.title: Four tankers struck by explosions in Strait of Hormuz, Iran says
headlines.summary: Four tankers hit in the Strait of Hormuz is the kind of headline that moves crude before the open — roughly 20% of global seaborne oil transits that chokepoint, and any escalation there is an instant bid for energy names and a tax on everything else. Layer in the Houthi attack on the Saudi East-West pipeline and Trump saying he doesn't need an Iran deal, and you've got a geopolitical premium that isn't going away quietly. Energy stocks, shipping names, and defense contractors all feel this one.
